description.value: In this design project, students investigate contemporary drivers of food trends to define a design opportunity within a professional culinary context. Students select a specific driver—such as sustainability, health and wellbeing, or cultural fusion—to guide the development of a designed solution. They apply divergent design thinking to generate and explore multiple concepts, evaluated against specific criteria: trend alignment, environmental sustainability, and aesthetic appearance. Through iterative refinement and the use of graphical representation techniques, students communicate a final dish design, justifying their decisions based on technical, environmental, and social factors. The production phase utilises virtual reality (VR) technology to simulate complex culinary workflows, allowing students to demonstrate production skills and manage safety and efficiency in a digital environment. Finally, students evaluate the success of their designed solution and the effectiveness of the virtual production process against the established design criteria.
description.aiNotes:
Task 1 – Identify the Driver (Define) 

Choose one modern driver of food trends to guide your design. 
Examples: 

Health and wellbeing (e.g. high-protein, low-sugar, plant-based) 

Environmental sustainability (e.g. local produce, minimal waste) 

Cultural fusion (e.g. mixing flavours or ingredients from different cultures) 

Convenience and lifestyle (e.g. meals for busy people, easy to prepare) 

Deliverable: 

A short paragraph explaining your chosen food trend driver 

 

Task 2 – Generate Ideas (Develop) 

Use divergent thinking to explore a wide range of ideas. 

Focus on one design criterion at a time. The 3 criteria are trend alignment, sustainability, appearance 

Create at least five different ideas for each criterion 

Use sketches, notes, or diagrams to show your thinking 

Deliverable: 

A3 page showing idea generation and exploration (sketches, annotations, mind maps) 

 

Task 3 – Combine and Refine 

Narrow down and improve your ideas. 

Combine your best elements into 2–3 refined concepts 

Justify why each concept could work for the restaurant 

Evaluate against the criteria to see which one best suits 

Deliverable: 

A3 page showing refined ideas with annotations and justifications 

 

Task 4 – Final Design (Deliver) 

Present your final dish design. 

Clearly show what the dish looks like (drawings, photos, or digital visuals) 

Explain how it reflects your chosen food trend driver 

Describe how it meets all three criteria 

Deliverable: 

A3 page showing your final concept with clear visuals and explanations 

 

Task 5 – Cook it in VR 

Create a video of you cooking a representation of the dish in VR.  

Evaluate how well your dish meets each design criterion 

Deliverable: 

Cooking video presentation

conditions.value: 2–3 A3 pages or equivalent digital media pages that may include annotated graphical representations

length.value: 4-5 A3 pages. 1 minute presentation of the final product.

resourcesAvailable.value:
• VR headsets (Meta Quest) and compatible hardware for immersive culinary simulation.
• Professional culinary simulation software with haptic feedback and physics-based ingredient interaction.
• Digital video recording and editing software for capturing and refining production sequences.
• Graphic representation tools (e.g. Adobe Creative Cloud, Canva, or CAD software) for 2D/3D design and storyboarding.

context.value: In this unit, students investigate the intersection of food specialisations and emerging technologies through the application of virtual reality (VR) in culinary contexts. Students explore how immersive digital environments can simulate kitchen safety, complex culinary techniques, and production workflows to improve efficiency and reduce resource waste. They examine the role of simulation in modern food industries, considering how virtual environments support skill development and ethical decision-making in high-risk or resource-intensive scenarios. Through the design process, students generate and represent original ideas for virtual cooking experiences, using graphical representation techniques and storyboards to communicate their design thinking. The unit emphasises innovation, user experience, and the strategic use of technologies to address contemporary challenges in food production and training for preferred futures.

toComplete.value:
Investigate a specific driver of contemporary food trends, such as sustainability, health and wellbeing, or cultural fusion, and analyse its impact on modern culinary innovation and emerging technologies.

Define a design opportunity within a professional culinary context and develop a detailed design brief that identifies client needs and project constraints.

Develop specific criteria for success, including sustainability factors, to evaluate the effectiveness of design ideas and the final solution.

Generate and represent a range of original meal concepts using graphical representation techniques and virtual reality (VR) prototyping to explore sensory and functional properties.

Select and justify a preferred design solution, documenting the iterative refinement process and the impact of technical, environmental, and social factors.

Produce a final design portfolio featuring annotated graphical representations, including rendered views and production plans that communicate the design intent.

Execute the production of the designed solution within a virtual reality environment, applying safe work practices and managing complex culinary workflows with efficiency.

Evaluate the success of the final dish and the effectiveness of the virtual production process against the established criteria for success.

Present a multimodal pitch and a recorded VR production sequence to stakeholders, reflecting on the role of innovation and emerging technologies in creating preferred food futures.

authenticationStrategies.label: You will be provided class time for task completion.
You will produce sections of the final response under supervised conditions.
You will provide documentation of your progress.
Your teacher will collect copies of your response and monitor at key junctures.
Your teacher will collect and annotate a draft.
Your teacher will conduct interviews or consultations as you develop the response.
You must submit a declaration of authenticity.
You will produce summaries during your response preparation.
Your teacher will conduct interviews after submission to clarify or explore aspects of your response.
Your teacher will compare the responses of students who have worked together in groups.
Your teacher will ensure class cross-marking occurs.
